column11: Sanhedrin 108a: ‘GEMARA: The Sages taught in a baraita: The members of the generation of the flood have no share in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “And He obliterated every living thing that was upon the face of the ground, from man to cattle to creeping animal to the birds of the heaven; and they were obliterated from the earth” (Genesis 7:23). “And He obliterated every living thing” indicates in this world, whereas “and they were obliterated from the earth” indicates for the World-to-Come; this is the statement of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: The members of the generation of the flood will neither live nor be judged, as it is stated: “My soul shall not abide [yadon] in man forever”…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Sanhedrin 108a) to illuminate his argument here (“and regarding the generation of the Flood, the Sages noted (Sanhedrin 108a) that the Holy One gave them a foretaste of the World to Come, mirroring the Sabbath which is a foretaste of the World to Come, perceiving...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: I dreamed [while residing in Izbica] that they were revealing to me certain matters concerning the root of my soul, and among those disclosures they were telling me that the generation of Mashiach will be the very same souls as the Generation of the Wilderness [and Mashiach embodies the soul of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, as cited in Raya Mehemna (Zohar III, 246b)], and they themselves are the selfsame souls as the Generation of the Flood [for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, was also present there, as taught in the Zohar (III, 216b) and stated in Chullin 139b: "for that he also (beshagam)" equals the gematria of Moses (345)].
column15: Yet nevertheless he was compelled to conceal them with him, as stated in Tractate Sanhedrin (108b): “‘And he sent forth the dove from him’—from here we derive that clean birds dwell with the righteous.” For clean birds are defined by not preying and mauling while eating, demonstrating recognition that the wine belongs to the owner while thanks is given to the server (Bava Kama 92b).

column11: Niddah 13a: ‘The Gemara discusses the matter itself. Rabbi Eliezer says: With regard to anyone who holds his penis and urinates, it is considered as though he is bringing a flood to the world. The Rabbis said to Rabbi Eliezer: But if one does not hold his penis, small drops are sprayed on his legs, and he appears as one whose penis has been severed. A man with that affliction is incapable of fathering children. People who see urine on his legs might suspect that he is suffering from that condition and as a result they will cast aspersions about his children and say that they are children born from a forbidden relationship [mamzerim].’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Niddah 13a) to illuminate his argument here (“And specifically the sin of the Flood generation in wasting seed, termed by our Sages (Niddah 13a) "children of the flood," meaning expanding action in vain without creating any enduring, genuine entity, which issued...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: Through the sin of youth in wasting seed and nocturnal emission, so long as one has not rectified it properly, it is difficult to be saved from alien thoughts that darken the light of the sun. For from those seminal drops, which are literal soul-parts as mentioned in sections 241 and 242, and as our Sages of blessed memory called them in Niddah (13a): 'slaughterers of children'— these are like the souls of the wicked that engender evil thoughts, as mentioned in section 239.
column15: While in the generation of Abraham our Father—the era of the “second child”—he would not have been considered righteous. Yet because at that hour he was righteous, he was saved from the Flood; as stated in Rosh Hashanah (16b): “The Holy One judges man only according to his deeds at that moment, as written: ‘where he is.’”

column13: Exodus 35:3 "You shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations" Parashat Vayakhel: "Though I sit in darkness, Hashem is a light unto me" Micah 7:8. Fire is awe, shining in the dark; but what does a candle achieve in bright daylight Chullin 60b for one to whom Havayah is his light, as in "For a sun and a shield is Hashem" and fire is the cooking rectification of all food; except that most fruits are eaten raw; and concerning wine there is a dispute whether raw is superior to cooked.
column15: And this is what the Midrash concludes: “And when did He repay them? At the erection of the Mishkan (Tabernacle), as it is written (Numbers 7:12): ‘And he that presented his offering on the first day...’” Meaning, there in the Mishkan they visibly witnessed how human mortal action unites with the infinite light of Hashem: namely, man saw that for the physical wealth he relinquished [for his sacrifice], a heavenly lion of fire descended and consumed it; and all these physical vessels and the Mishkan were merely outer garments for the place of the Ark, which miraculously took up no physical space.

column13: And in the first chapter of Megillah (12a): "The protocol of Torah is that eating exceeds drinking," meaning what the Sages taught in Pirkei Avot (3:9): "Whosoever's deeds exceed his wisdom, his wisdom endures."
column15: For true unity flourishes only when dedicated to Heavenly honor, Hashem guaranteeing that within every gathering for Heaven’s sake His presence dwells, as in Avot (3:6): “Even two who sit and engage in Torah, the Shechinah rests between them”; while the gathering of the wicked is dispersion, as in Sanhedrin (26a): “A conspiracy of the wicked is not counted.”

column15: And in Zohar Pekudei (267a): And here stands the harlot to entice the foolish—from which it likewise indicates that the female is the enticer. And see Likutei Torah of the Ari (Psalms 18): Know that the males are the masters of the sword and slaying, for such is nature that males are warriors; whereas the females entice man to sin; first descend the forces drawn from the female aspect of evil to seduce man, coming as females alone, for the male has not the power to seduce like the female.

column11: Zohar, Vayakhel 1:2-11: ‘Subsequently, however, the sections separated, each betaking itself to its own affinity, and so the mixed multitude made the golden calf and led astray numbers who afterwards died, and thus brought upon Israel death and slaughter. The Holy One, blessed be He, then said: “Henceforward the work of the Tabernacle shall be performed from the side of Israel only.” Straightway “Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel… Take ye from among you an offering unto the Lord” (Ibid. 35, 1-5). “From among you” emphatically, but not “from every man whose heart maketh him willing”, as in the previous injunction. Furthermore, as no place of assembly is mentioned, the words, “And…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8, Rav Tzadok cites this kabbalistic teaching (Zohar, Vayakhel 1:2-11) to illuminate his argument here (“And as written in the Zohar (Exodus 195a): "And Moses assembled" denotes separating them from the mixed multitude, congregating Israel alone, the mixed multitude having no portion in the House of our God, for the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And in the Zohar's introduction (2a): those who sinned with the calf said so based on this mystery, see there, for they severed Elehe ("these") from Elohim, which connects with Mi ("Who"—the Binah of the heart) because it stands to be questioned. The meaning: Binah in the heart is hidden and concealed, subject to questioning ("Who"), whereas physical deeds are tangible, pointing visibly to "these" (eleh), where asking "who is this" does not apply.
column15: Meaning that the Blessed Name seals His Name upon this person whose heart continually embodies prayer even when not actively verbalizing petitions, fulfilling: “And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication, be near unto the Lord” (I Kings 8:59), the prayer praying of itself continuously, as in: “and prayer shall be made for him continually” (Psalms 72:15).

column11: Zohar, Shemot: ‘From which it is evident that all the righteous are known by all in those higher regions before their souls descend into this world; how much more, then, Moses. We also learn from this that the souls of the righteous emanate from an upper region, as we have already stated. But there is also an esoteric lesson connected with it, namely, that the soul has a father and a mother, as the body has a father and a mother in this world. In fact, all things above and below proceed from Male and Female, as we have already derived from the words “Let the earth bring forth a living soul” (Gen. 1, 24). “The earth” symbolizes the community of Israel; “a living soul”-the soul of the first, the supernal…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8, Rav Tzadok cites this kabbalistic teaching (Zohar, Shemot) to illuminate his argument here (“And as written in the Zohar (Exodus 195a): "And Moses assembled" denotes separating them from the mixed multitude, congregating Israel alone, the mixed multitude having no portion in the House of our God, for the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And at the beginning of the Exodus from Egypt Amalek assaulted them, and at the end of the generation of the wilderness the idolatry of Pe'or assaulted them; and then they completed the subjugation of the entire structure of the idolatry of the nations. And the error of the Golden Calf had no connection to pagan idolatry, God forbid; nor did they mock the words of the Sages, God forbid, but on the contrary believed deeply in Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him.
column15: And as stated in the Zohar (Beshalach 54a): Lest you say, since the soul will be on a supremely exalted level, it will not wish to humble itself to descend into the body at the Resurrection of the Dead? Concerning this the Zohar replies there: Go out and learn from the first beginning, for all those spirits and souls that were in the highest supernal rung the Holy One brought down to the earth below.

And in Creation: the twenty-two...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: As written: "For You also have wrought all our works for us" (Isaiah 26:12). And since we are sanctified unto His Name from birth, womb, and conception without our prior knowledge, His seal rests upon all actions wrought through us as having been for His glory, though in this world this remains veiled. Therefore the Talmud states in Rosh Hashanah (17a): "Gehinnom is consumed, but they are not consumed," for as long as Gehinnom endures it is still termed "this world."
column15: “Make you an ark of gopher wood, etc.” The nature of this counsel corresponds to Zohar Noach (68a): Rabbi Chiyya opened: “‘Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him?’ Come and see: when a man sins before his Master and seeks to conceal himself, the Holy One executes judgment upon him publicly; but when a man purifies himself, the Holy One desires to hide him so he not be seen on the day of wrath, as written: ‘Hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast.’”

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 12:4: ‘Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya, Rabbi Yehuda says: “The heavens and the earth…were completed” (Genesis 2:1) – at their designated time. “And their entire host” (Genesis 2:1) – at their designated time. Rabbi Neḥemya said to him: But is it not written: “These are the outgrowths of the heavens and of the earth when they were created [on the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens]” – which teaches that on the same day they were created they produced their outgrowths? He said to him: But is it not written: “It was evening, it was morning, one day…a second day…a third day…a fourth day…a fifth day…a sixth day”? Rabbi Neḥemya said: They are like people picking figs; each one of…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 8, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 12:4) to illuminate his argument here (“And in truth all was created on the first day (Bereishit Rabbah 12:4), with the utterance "Let there be light" all forms of light were created, the lights within vessels being emanated, their ultimate completion...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: Which is the primal dust beneath the Throne of Glory from which stems the preservative kav, intermingling with the wheat that hints at the twenty-two letters of the Written Torah, the reflection of Supernal Wisdom, which comprise nine sefirotic attributes, each subdivided into ten within the masculine aspect and ten within the feminine, yielding 180, and one kav in a kor (which contains 180 kav) is exactly 1/180th, representing the very threshold of the gate of fear: Malchut of Malchut in Knesset Yisrael, the dry and salty earth.
column15: “These are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens.” And in Midrash Rabbah (Bereishit 12:15) it is taught: A parable of a king who had fragile glass cups; the king said: “If I pour boiling water into them, they will burst; if ice-cold water, they will crack”; what did the king do? He mixed hot with cold, poured it in, and they endured.

column13: And as they said there: "It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that there was no one in his generation like him"; and it stated with precision "the One Who spoke and the world came into being," because he attained the root of the light at the inception of the world's creation in the utterance "Let there be light" (Bereishis 1:3), which is the light of the Torah concealed for the righteous in the Future; which in this world became clothed through man's enclothing in "garments of skin" (kasnos or with an ayin, Bereishis 3:21), the physical body that garments the soul.
column15: Whereas light, living animal soul, and man who is a speaking spirit—all three are absolute novelties, and therefore “and it was so” is omitted. Afterward, however, concerning vegetation given for food it is written: “and it was so” — meaning that nature itself developed until it became designated sustenance for man, food having an intrinsic soul-connection to the one who consumes it; hence “and it was so” is written.

column11: Chagigah 11b: ‘§ The Gemara continues to clarify the mishna, which reads: One may not expound the topic of forbidden sexual relations before three individuals. What is the reason for this? If we say it is because it is written: “None of you [ish, ish] shall approach any near of kin to uncover their nakedness” (Leviticus 18:6). Ish, ish, literally means: Man, man. It is understood as an allusion to the number of students permitted to study the topic. This is as it is explained immediately: “Man, man” equals two; “any near of kin to him” is one; and the Merciful One states: “You shall not approach to uncover their nakedness,” which indicates that one may not expound the halakhot of forbidden sexual…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 9, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Chagigah 11b) to illuminate his argument here (“The mystical secret of the Account of Creation concerning which the Mishnah states "one does not expound" Chagigah 11b, Rashi explained found in Ein Yaakov, beginning of chapter 2 of Chagigah, though omitted from...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And this is designated "visions of G-d" in Ezekiel, where perception proceeds not from the created effect but from the transcendent Cause; namely, because "Hashem's portion is His people" and the soul unites so intimately with its Maker that it becomes one with Him, perceiving reality from His vantage point. Therefore, "one does not expound..." (Chagigah 11b), for in the Work of Creation there are two: Creator and created, and one does not expound to two besides the teacher (which would make three), reflecting a breakdown of divine unity; but within the awareness of the Creator there exist only two: Creator and creation.

column13: And not in water (as written at the end of Sanhedrin 67b: that they tested it upon water); and sorcery mirrors the alien woman; while in permissible holiness—it mirrors Sefer Yetzirah, concerning which they stated in Sanhedrin 65b that it is blameless and permitted; and even in this they taught: “Sanctify yourself in that which is permitted to you”; and so they taught in Kiddushin 71a concerning divine Names.
column15: And this is (Genesis 2:24): “Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, etc.” — meaning that he must not heed merely what Chochmah (Father) and Binah (Mother) dictate to him—namely, that he should avoid entering moral doubt, avoid pursuing her, and remain himself in pure clarity; not so, but rather “and shall cleave unto his wife”—meaning he must humble himself to her level, trusting that He to whom all belongs will come and redeem them both.

column11: Sanhedrin 65b: ‘Turnus Rufus said to him: This is what I mean to say to you: Who is to say that now is Shabbat? Perhaps a different day of the week is Shabbat. Rabbi Akiva said to him: The Sabbatyon River can prove that today is Shabbat, as it is calm only on Shabbat. A necromancer can also prove this, as the dead do not rise on Shabbat. The grave of his father, referring to Turnus Rufus’s father, can also prove this, as it does not emit smoke on Shabbat, although smoke rises from it all week, as during the week he is being punished in Gehenna. Turnus Rufus said to him: You have demeaned my father, you have publicly shamed him, and you have cursed him by saying that he is being punished in Gehenna.’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 9, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Sanhedrin 65b) to illuminate his argument here (“Rav Chanina and Rav Oshaya engaged in Sefer Yetzirah every Sabbath eve, and there was created for them a three-year-old calf, and they ate it" ibid., Rashi's explanation being: it was created automatically on its...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And "Name" (shem) is Will (ratzon), the numerical value of Shemo (346) equaling Ratzon (346), His powers being His Will. And the Torah is His Will, as in the rabbinic phrase: "Who spoke and His will was done." And so the first three blessings of the Amidah express what His Will is. And since the Blessed Name wills to support the fallen, He will certainly support them, even though the fallen one lacks the strength and consciousness to plead for himself to awaken that Will.
column15: “And God said, Let us make man.” The garment of man is the window through which each soul beholds the Blessed Name according to its individual soul-root. And so we find regarding the Prophets, who perceived the Blessed Name through diverse garments and varied visions; for although it is written (Isaiah 6:3): “The whole earth is full of His glory,” it is through the specific window established by Hashem through which He is overtly perceived that the prophetic vision takes place.

column11: Sefer Yetzirah 1:1: ‘YAH, ADONAI of Hosts, God of Israel, Living God and King of the World, EL SHADDAI, Merciful and Gracious, High and Exalted, Dwelling Ever Above, Holy Is His Name—He carved 'Work of Creation' is not the abstract verb bara 'to create' used in [Genesis 1:1]. Instead, the SY prefers verbs relating to the processes of craftsman and artisans, in particular stonemasons: chaqaq 'to carve, chisel', chatzav 'to hew', shaqal 'to weigh', yasad 'to found', yatzar 'to form, shape, fashion'—the latter providing the name of the book, Sefer Yetzirah, literally the 'Book of Forming' but conventionally rendered the 'Book of Creation'. and created His World 'and created His World' in this verse. In these…’ Context and connection to Likkutei Maamarim: In Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 9, Rav Tzadok cites this kabbalistic teaching (Sefer Yetzirah 1:1) to illuminate his argument here (“And this explains the teaching: "with three books: Sefer (text), Sephar (number), and Sippur (telling)" Sefer Yetzirah 1:1: as is known, there exist three classes of letters in the Torah, for there are also large...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source grounds the spiritual dynamic of Torah, Israel's sanctity, and divine service developed in this discourse of Likkutei Maamarim.
column13: And this was the manifestation of the primordial depth of light that was revealed at the Exodus from Egypt; emerging through the ongoing spiritual toil in remembering the Exodus from Egypt which Israel perform in each and every year; so that the light emerges little by little from concealment until arriving at consummate revelation, meriting eternal life; wherefore the Resurrection of the Dead will occur on Pesach, and we read this as the Haftarah on the intermediate Sabbath of Pesach (Yechezkel 37).
column15: Meaning supernal worlds are compounded of two rungs: male and female, receiving force and bestowing force, lights and vessels. As in Isaiah 6:3: “And one called unto another,” rendered: “and they receive one from another,” each receiving from above and bestowing below.
